Cluster_AKAP8_1.paragraph: This system includes multiple components of the circadian clock (PER2, PER3, CRY2, NR1D1), which regulate daily oscillations of gene expression in metabolic tissues. These transcriptional regulators control the rhythmic expression of key metabolic enzymes and transporters, thereby orchestrating the timing of energy storage, mobilization, and hormonal signaling across the light-dark cycle. Their co-presence with nutrient transporters and signaling proteins suggests functional integration in time-dependent metabolic homeostasis.
Cluster_AKAP8_1.keyword: ("PER2" OR "PER3" OR "CRY2" OR "NR1D1") AND ("circadian" OR "metabolic" OR "homeostasis") AND (hasabstract[text]) AND humans[mh] NOT Retracted Publication[pt]
references: Liu, Zhihua, Chu, Guiyan. "Chronobiology in mammalian health." Molecular biology reports, 2013, pp. 2491-501, doi: https://doi.org/10.1007/s11033-012-2330-4

Cluster_AKAP8_2.paragraph: Key metabolic effectors such as INSR (insulin receptor), SLC2A4 (GLUT4), and ADCY5 (adenylate cyclase 5) are central to insulin-stimulated glucose uptake in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue. SLC2A4 translocates to the membrane in response to insulin signaling via INSR, facilitating glucose entry into cells. ADCY5 contributes to cAMP-mediated modulation of insulin secretion and signaling. These proteins form a coordinated module that transduces insulin signals to regulate glucose utilization, strongly linking this system to energy metabolism.
Cluster_AKAP8_2.keyword: ("INSR" OR "SLC2A4" OR "ADCY5") AND ("glucose uptake" OR "insulin signaling" OR "energy metabolism") AND (hasabstract[text]) AND humans[mh] NOT Retracted Publication[pt]
references: Højlund, Kurt. "Metabolism and insulin signaling in common metabolic disorders and inherited insulin resistance." Danish medical journal, 2014, pp. B4890.

Cluster_AKAP8_3.paragraph: Genes like FAAH (fatty acid amide hydrolase), DAGLA (diacylglycerol lipase alpha), DGKD (diacylglycerol kinase delta), SREBF1 (a transcriptional regulator of lipid biosynthesis), and COQ10A (coenzyme Q10 biosynthesis) contribute to lipid signaling and storage. Their integration suggests the system supports lipid flux coordination, particularly in metabolically active tissues where insulin and circadian signals converge.

references: Geng, Feng, Guo, Deliang. "SREBF1/SREBP-1 concurrently regulates lipid synthesis and lipophagy to maintain lipid homeostasis and tumor growth." Autophagy, 2024, pp. 1183-1185, doi: https://doi.org/10.1080/15548627.2023.2275501

Cluster_AKAP8_4.paragraph: Solute carrier proteins (SLC22A5, SLC45A3, SLC46A1) and enzymes like L2HGDH and CKMT2 indicate participation in mitochondrial metabolism and organic solute transport. These molecules sustain energy production by managing the import and export of critical cofactors, such as carnitine (SLC22A5), which is essential for fatty acid β-oxidation. CKMT2 couples ATP production to energy-demanding processes in tissues like heart and muscle.

Cluster_AKAP8_5.paragraph: DEPTOR, a regulator of mTOR signaling, functions as a metabolic rheostat under nutrient availability and insulin conditions. Trafficking proteins like HOOK2, GGA3, and PITPNM2 contribute to endosomal sorting and membrane dynamics, processes essential for glucose transporter recycling and hormonal signal propagation. These components ensure that signaling and nutrient uptake are tightly coupled with membrane trafficking pathways.

Cluster_AKAP8_6.paragraph: Proteins like JAG1 (a Notch ligand) and LRP5 (a Wnt co-receptor involved in metabolic tissue homeostasis) suggest developmental regulation of metabolic tissue architecture and function. AMIGO1 and PLEKHA7 also influence cellular structure and junctional stability, potentially affecting tissue responsiveness to hormonal and circadian cues.

Cluster_PKM_1.paragraph: This system prominently features components regulated by or regulating hypoxia-inducible factors (HIFs). HIF1A, EGLN1, EGLN3, MIR210HG, VEGFA, BNIP3, and DDIT4 are core mediators of the transcriptional and metabolic response to low oxygen conditions. EGLNs hydroxylate HIF1A under normoxia, while HIF1A activates genes that enhance glycolytic flux, angiogenesis (VEGFA), and survival during hypoxic stress (BNIP3, MIR210HG). DDIT4 connects hypoxia to mTOR inhibition, reducing energy expenditure. These factors establish a functional axis adapting metabolism and signaling to oxygen availability.
